brief.headline: Push to ₹0.65–0.80/pc for caps at higher volume — market shows headroom — and qualify Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a second source.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a revised quote in the ₹0.65–0.80/pc band for the 28 mm PP cap (and similar items) at our current or higher volume.
priceAsk.basis: Market asking prices for this cap run ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc. The market verdict says 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec' — so at our scale a lower band is justified.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Hold at 30 days after receipt — already reasonable, and moving faster offers little value to us here.

brief.financialLeverage: Suraj publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue, profit or how tight their cash is. Our ₹58.17 L annual spend is material for a private converter, but without their numbers we can't gauge exactly how much. That means we lean on the market data and on lining up a credible second source to create competition. Because we don't know their financial strength, avoid a hard squeeze that could destabilise supply — instead, frame the price ask around market benchmarks and the value of a long-term partnership at higher volume.

evidence.point: We spend ₹58.17 L a year with them — enough volume to earn better-than-typical pricing.
Market asking prices for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap sit between ₹0.55 and ₹1.20 per piece, typically ₹0.85–0.95.
The market verdict confirms 'modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec' — so a lower band is realistic.
We already pay 30 days after receipt — not the worst terms — so cash freed by faster payment is small.
evidence.figure: 30 Days After Receipt; ₹4.78 L freed if moved to immediate, ₹2.39 L if 15 days faster

evidence.point: Suraj's financials are not public, so we build our ask on our own purchase data and the market line.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate, already qualified for packaging.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) for pails, containers, pharma — strong, profitable, robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (lead to qualify)
alternates.why: A manufacturer lead (pan-India, medium confidence) from public research — verify capability and MOQ before sending an RFQ.

risks: Suraj publishes no financials — we can't see if they're healthy or stretched, so watch for any supply hiccups and avoid pushing so hard we destabilise them.
The market ask verdict says 'modest headroom' — if they resist ₹0.65–0.80, be ready to tie the lower price to a volume commitment or a longer contract.
We have strong listed alternates (Manjushree, Mold-Tek) but they may have higher MOQs or longer lead times — qualify one now so we're not caught if Suraj pushes back hard.
The market-backup leads (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, others) are unverified — treat them as research pointers, not approved sources, until we audit them.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're consolidating our rigid-packaging spend and want to lock in a long-term partnership with you — let's discuss a price in the ₹0.65–0.80 range for our cap volumes, in line with what the market supports at scale.
